title: Hellraiser service rifle
paint:
A stamped-steel long-stroke assault rifle, the most common rifle pattern in the world. Pose: rifle diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 85% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: a stamped steel receiver with a ribbed dust cover on top; a long gas tube above the barrel with a wooden upper handguard; a strongly curved, ribbed 30-round box magazine; a slanted muzzle brake; a tangent rear sight just in front of the dust cover and a front sight post on a triangular base near the muzzle; a large lever safety on the right side of the receiver; a wooden lower handguard, a separate pistol grip and a fixed wooden stock with a slight drop. Materials: dark blued and parkerised steel, warm reddish-brown wood with worn edges, steel rubbed bright at the edges and the magazine lips. Maker's touch: one muted oxide-red band (#CC2435) painted round the lower handguard. No bayonet.
At 32 px: the curved magazine, the gas tube over the barrel and the dropped wooden stock.

title: Service pistol
paint:
A polymer-frame striker-fired service pistol, the pistol in every holster. Pose: side profile turned slightly toward the viewer, muzzle right, level, filling about 80% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: a blocky, squared steel slide with a flat top, squared front and fine vertical serrations at the rear; a small open ejection port; a polymer frame with a squared trigger guard; a trigger with a small safety blade in its face; no hammer showing; a slightly angled grip with shallow finger grooves and a flush magazine base. Materials: matte black slide with edges rubbed grey, black polymer frame. Maker's touch: one faded blue-grey (#5394AC) grip panel set into the side of the grip.
At 32 px: a plain blocky slide on a squared frame, no hammer.

title: Magistrate heavy pistol
paint:
A steel single-action heavy service pistol of the century-old pattern. Pose: side profile turned slightly toward the viewer, muzzle right, level, filling about 80% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: a slim, full-length flat-sided steel slide with vertical serrations at the rear; a short round barrel bushing at the muzzle, flush with the slide (no flare); a spur hammer at the back; a grip safety in the back of the grip with a beavertail; a thumb safety lever above the grip; a straight, near-vertical grip with flat side panels; a slim rounded trigger guard and a long flat trigger. Materials: polished dark blued steel with worn bright edges. Maker's touch: ivory grip panels with one small blank brass seal plate set in them.
At 32 px: a long slim flat slide over a straight grip with pale panels.

title: Decrkm auto-pistol
paint:
A full-size select-fire burst machine pistol with a fold-down front grip. Pose: side profile turned slightly toward the viewer, muzzle right, level, filling about 80% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: a steel pistol with an open-top slide that shows the barrel; a short three-port compensator on the muzzle; an enlarged trigger guard; a small metal front grip hinged in front of the trigger guard and folded down, pointing to the ground; a long 20-round magazine reaching well below the grip; an exposed hammer. Materials: dark gunmetal, black grip panels, worn bright edges. Maker's touch: one small brass pin through the slide.
At 32 px: a pistol with a long magazine and a little grip hanging under its front.

title: Decrkm SMG
paint:
A compact boxy telescoping-bolt submachine gun, the little SMG of every desert war. Pose: diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 70% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: a short, square, boxy stamped receiver; the straight magazine inserted through the pistol grip; a grip safety at the back of the grip; a short barrel with a knurled barrel nut at the front of the receiver; a ribbed top cover with a cocking knob on top; a folding metal stock folded forward under the receiver, its butt plate just behind the muzzle. Materials: gunmetal and worn black paint, black polymer grip. Maker's touch: none, no colour accent: bare worn gunmetal.
At 32 px: a small square box with the magazine coming out of the grip.

title: Legion PDW
paint:
The compact modern personal defence weapon with the long magazine through the pistol grip, the folding front grip and the two-rod sliding stock. Pose: diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 70% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: a short, tall, slab-sided polymer receiver whose top line steps down at the front, the tall part ending above the trigger guard and the lower front sloping forward to a short barrel that sticks out a hand's width; a full-length rail along the top with a small flip-up rear sight at the back and a flip-up front sight at the front; a T-shaped charging handle at the very back of the top; a pistol grip set well back, raked slightly, with a long straight magazine inserted through it and sticking out a good way below the grip; a large squared trigger guard; a vertical front grip hinged under the front of the receiver, folded down; a telescoping stock of two thin parallel rods with a small flat butt plate, pulled out to full length behind the receiver. Materials: olive-grey polymer and dark steel, anonymous and mass-produced. Maker's touch: none, no colour accent.
At 32 px: a short tall box with a long magazine dropping out of the grip, a front grip hanging under it and two thin rods behind; nothing lies on top of it.

title: Mandestra drum-gun
paint:
The classic drum-fed submachine gun of the old gang wars. Pose: diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 70% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: a finned (ribbed) barrel with a slotted compensator on its tip; a vertical wooden front grip under the barrel; a big round drum magazine under the receiver just in front of the trigger guard; a flat-sided receiver with a cocking knob on top; a wooden pistol grip; a fixed wooden stock. Materials: lacquered red-black finish on the metal, dark wood. Maker's touch: brass plates on the face of the drum, blank.
At 32 px: a round drum, a vertical front grip and a finned barrel.

title: Long rifle
paint:
The classic military and police bolt-action precision rifle in a one-piece synthetic stock. Pose: rifle diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 85% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: a one-piece synthetic stock with a straight comb, a near-vertical pistol grip, a deep wide fore-end and a thick rubber butt pad; a round cylindrical receiver with a turned-down bolt handle and a round knob on the right; a hinged floorplate flush under the stock, nothing hanging below; a long heavy round barrel, plain to a flat crown, no muzzle brake and no iron sights; a large long scope with tall adjustment turrets in two rings; a bipod folded under the front of the fore-end. Materials: matte olive-drab stock speckled darker, black matte steel, scuffed. Maker's touch: none, neutral matte.
At 32 px: a long heavy plain barrel, a big scope and a deep one-piece stock with no magazine showing.

title: .700 Blackpoint anti-materiel
paint:
A huge semi-automatic anti-materiel rifle, the biggest rifle a person can fire. Pose: diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 90% of the canvas width, drawn dense and heavy. Silhouette, kept exactly: a very long flat two-part receiver; a long heavy barrel ending in a large arrowhead-shaped double-chamber muzzle brake; a top rail with a big scope; a carry handle; a folding bipod at the front of the receiver; a box magazine; a big recoil pad on the butt. Materials: grim dark grey steel, worn. Maker's touch: none; the muzzle brake scorched dark.
At 32 px: a very long flat rifle with an arrowhead muzzle and a bipod.

title: CCEC marksman rifle
paint:
The classic long, slim short-stroke-piston semi-automatic marksman rifle. Pose: rifle diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 85% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: a long slim milled receiver; a short-stroke gas piston in a slim gas tube above a long thin barrel; a slotted flash hider; slotted handguards; a skeleton thumbhole stock with an open frame and a cheek rest; a long scope mounted offset on a side rail; a short, slightly curved 10-round box magazine. Materials: ivory polymer furniture, dark steel. Maker's touch: one thin blue-grey stripe (#5394AC) along the stock.
At 32 px: a long thin rifle with an open skeleton stock and a scope.

title: Adamantile battle rifle
paint:
The tilting-breechblock metric battle rifle with the long slotted flash hider, the right arm of half the world's armies. Pose: rifle diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 85% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: a long slim receiver whose top cover tapers down at the back to a rear peep sight; a small folding cocking handle on the left side of the receiver, toward its front; a straight 20-round box magazine with a slight forward lean, set ahead of the trigger guard; a separate, steeply raked pistol grip; a slim handguard flaring wider at the back, with ventilation slots along it; a tall front sight post with two protective ears near the muzzle; a long slotted flash hider; a fixed stock in line with the receiver with a ribbed butt plate. No carry handle. Materials: dark steel and black furniture. Maker's touch: one small blank gilt boss at the heel of the stock and a thin brass-orange (#F68A38) trim line; no plates.
At 32 px: a long straight rifle with a straight magazine, a tall eared front sight and a long slotted flash hider.

title: Hellraiser LMG
paint:
The light machine gun of the stamped long-stroke rifle family: the line's service rifle lengthened. Pose: diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 90% of the canvas width, drawn dense and heavy. Silhouette, kept exactly: the same stamped receiver as the line's service rifle, with the ribbed dust cover and the large lever safety on the right; a long, heavier barrel running far past the handguard, with a plain slotted muzzle device; a folding bipod hinged near the muzzle, its two legs folded back along the barrel; a long gas tube with a wooden upper handguard and a wooden lower handguard; a long, strongly curved ribbed box magazine (longer than the rifle's); a tangent rear sight on the receiver; a fixed wooden stock with a deep club-foot butt. Materials: dark blued and parkerised steel, warm reddish-brown wood with hard scratches. Maker's touch: one muted oxide-red band (#CC2435) round the lower handguard. No trench spikes.
At 32 px: the service rifle's shape made long, with a bipod at the muzzle, a long curved magazine and a club-foot stock.

title: Lumeri scattergun
paint:
A pump-action combat shotgun, the shotgun in every patrol car. Pose: diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 80% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: a long tube magazine under the barrel; a ribbed pump fore-end on the tube; a receiver with a side ejection port; a bead front sight; a plain fixed stock with a straight wrist. Materials: ivory-painted wood, dark steel. Maker's touch: one thin Lumeri gold (#F2C46A) inlay line along the stock.
At 32 px: a long barrel over a tube, with a ribbed pump.

title: Brigade auto-shotgun
paint:
A box-fed semi-automatic shotgun on the stamped long-stroke rifle's body. Pose: diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 80% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: the stamped receiver with a ribbed dust cover and a large lever safety on the right; a fat, straight box magazine; a short gas tube over the barrel; a thick barrel; a separate pistol grip; a side-folding stock, extended. Materials: dark steel and black polymer. Maker's touch: one small blank gilt boss on the stock and a thin brass-orange (#F68A38) trim line; no plates.
At 32 px: the stamped rifle body with a fat straight magazine and a thick barrel.

title: Smetanita thumper
paint:
A single-shot break-action 40 mm grenade launcher, the classic shoulder-fired one. Pose: diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 90% of the canvas width. Materials: lacquered black metal, dark wood. Maker's touch: brass on the hinge and one small blank brass tag on the stock.
At 32 px: a fat stubby barrel on a slim wooden stock, with a leaf sight on top.

title: Breacher tube
paint:
A reusable shoulder-fired recoilless rifle. Pose: diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 90% of the canvas width, drawn dense and heavy. Silhouette, kept exactly: a long fat tube; a flared venturi cone at the rear; a front grip under the front half; a pistol grip with the trigger under the middle; a padded shoulder rest; a side optic on a bracket on the left. Materials: olive-drab tube, black grips. Maker's touch: one pale stripe painted round the tube near the muzzle.
At 32 px: a fat tube with a flared rear, two grips and a side sight.

title: Frontier hand cannon
paint:
A big double-action magnum revolver, the detective's hand cannon. Pose: side profile turned slightly toward the viewer, muzzle right, level, filling about 80% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: a long barrel with a full-length underlug beneath it and a vented top rib; a large fluted six-chamber cylinder; an adjustable rear sight; an exposed hammer; a rubber-wrapped grip with finger grooves. title: ADCorp line rifle (the line's base)
paint:
A modular light assault rifle in the classic straight-line layout. Pose: rifle diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 85% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: the stock, the buffer tube and the barrel all on one straight line; a two-part receiver (a flat-top upper with a full-length top rail, a separate lower with a flared magazine well); a slightly curved 30-round box magazine; a tall triangular A-frame front sight post over the gas block; a small flip-up rear sight on the rail; a forward assist bump and a round ejection-port cover on the right of the upper; a sliding six-position stock on a round tube; a round ribbed handguard; a birdcage flash hider; a separate pistol grip. Materials: black anodised metal and black polymer, rubbed grey at the edges and the magazine lips. Maker's touch: one small blank tag in muted vermilion (#C4553A) clipped to the sling loop at the stock.
At 32 px: the straight line from stock to muzzle, the triangle front sight and the curved magazine.

title: ADCorp short carbine
paint:
The same modular rifle cut down for close quarters. Pose: diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 70% of the canvas width like the submachine guns. Silhouette, kept exactly: the straight-line layout, the flat-top upper with a full-length rail and the flared magazine well of the modular rifle, but a very short barrel that ends just past a short free-float rail handguard with slots along its sides; a short angled foregrip; a compact sliding stock collapsed all the way in; a curved 30-round box magazine; a short flash hider; a small red-dot optic on the rail and no front sight post. Materials: black anodised metal and black polymer, edges worn grey. Maker's touch: one small blank tag in muted vermilion (#C4553A) on the sling loop.
At 32 px: the line rifle's body with almost no barrel, a collapsed stock and a dot sight.

title: ADCorp designated rifle

The modular rifle grown into a full-power semi-automatic marksman rifle. Pose: rifle diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 85% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: the straight-line two-part receiver of the modular rifle but larger and deeper; a long heavy free-floating barrel inside a long slim free-float rail handguard; a straight 20-round box magazine (not curved); a long scope in two rings on the top rail; a fixed adjustable precision stock with a raised cheek piece; a folded bipod under the handguard; a short muzzle brake. Materials: black and dark earth-brown polymer and anodised metal, scuffed. Maker's touch: one small blank tag in muted vermilion (#C4553A) on the stock's sling loop.
At 32 px: the straight-line modular body, long and scoped, with a straight magazine.

title: Chezknov battle rifle (the line's base)

A roller-delayed full-power battle rifle. Pose: rifle diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 85% of the canvas width. title: Chezknov machine carbine

A roller-delayed submachine gun, the slim classic of every counter-terror team. Pose: diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 70% of the canvas width like the submachine guns. title: Chezknov precision rifle

The roller-delayed rifle made into a heavy semi-automatic precision rifle. Pose: rifle diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 85% of the canvas width. title: Arsenal piston rifle (the line's base)
paint:
A modern short-stroke piston modular assault rifle. Pose: rifle diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 85% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: a long one-piece aluminium upper receiver with a continuous top rail from the back to the muzzle and short rails on the sides; a reciprocating charging handle on the left of the upper; an angular polymer lower with a flared magazine well; a slightly curved box magazine; a side-folding telescoping polymer stock with a stepped angular cheek riser, extended; a prong flash hider; folded flip-up iron sights. Maker's touch: one thin blue-grey trim line (#5394AC) along the lower edge of the stock.
At 32 px: the long flat upper with a rail all the way, a sand two-tone body and an angular stock.

title: Arsenal courier PDW
paint:
A compact top-fed bullpup personal defence weapon. Pose: diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 70% of the canvas width like the submachine guns. Silhouette, kept exactly: one smooth sculpted polymer body with rounded edges; a long flat translucent smoke-grey magazine lying horizontally along the whole top of the gun, with the small cartridges inside it seen lying sideways; a thumbhole-style grip with a large trigger-guard opening and a second hole in front for the support hand; a short barrel with a small flash hider; a small reflex sight above the front of the magazine. Materials: dark green-black polymer, the magazine smoke-grey and translucent. Maker's touch: one thin blue-grey trim line (#5394AC) along the butt.
At 32 px: a rounded body with a flat bar lying on top of it and a hole for the hand.

title: Arsenal heavy rifle

The piston rifle in full-power precision form. Pose: rifle diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 85% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: the same long one-piece upper with a continuous top rail and the angular lower as the piston rifle, larger; a long heavy barrel; a straight 20-round box magazine; a fixed precision stock with an adjustable cheek piece and an adjustable butt plate in the same angular stepped style; a long scope; a folded bipod; a muzzle brake. Materials: sand-coloured polymer and anodised metal, black barrel and magazine. Maker's touch: one thin blue-grey trim line (#5394AC) along the stock.
At 32 px: the piston rifle, longer and scoped, with a straight magazine and a fixed stock.

title: Smetanita pocket pistol

title: Albert Town service rifle (the line's base)

title: Albert Town brush carbine
paint:
A semi-automatic wood carbine with a folding blade bayonet. Pose: diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 70% of the canvas width like the short guns. Silhouette, kept exactly: a one-piece wooden stock with a straight wrist; a fixed box magazine that is a shallow bulge just in front of the trigger guard (no detachable magazine hanging down); a gas tube over the barrel ending at a hooded front sight; a folding blade bayonet hinged under the muzzle, folded back under the barrel against the wood; a tangent rear sight; a bolt handle on the right side of the receiver. At 32 px: a short wood carbine with a blade folded under its barrel and no hanging magazine.

title: Albert Town stalking rifle
paint:
The classic full-stocked bolt-action stalking rifle. Pose: rifle diagonal, about 16 degrees, muzzle up and right, filling about 85% of the canvas width. Silhouette, kept exactly: a figured walnut stock running the full length of the short barrel to the muzzle, ending in a steel nose cap, with a raised cheek piece and a pistol-grip cap; a flat, spoon-shaped bolt handle swept back along the stock; a short barrel with a small folding leaf rear sight and a bead front sight at the nose cap; a small hunting scope in two low rings; a hinged floorplate with no magazine hanging below; a leather sling with two swivels.
